nodes.title: Bigquery: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Bigquery. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: A retail company tracks billions of product view events per day. Analysts need t?
flashcards.back: Materialized views precompute and store query results, automatically refreshing on new data. For repetitive aggregation queries over a rolling 7-day window by category, they eliminate redundant computation. BI Engine accelerates ad-hoc queries but is better for interactive dashboards. Partitioning/clustering helps scan cost but does not precompute aggregates. Bigtable is for key-value lookups, not analytical aggregation.

flashcards.front: A healthcare company needs to load 10 years of patient visit records stored as A?
flashcards.back: BigQuery load jobs are the recommended way to bulk-load static data from Cloud Storage. They are free (no charge per byte loaded), support Avro natively with automatic schema detection, and are fast for large datasets. Streaming inserts are charged per byte and suited for real-time data, not historical bulk loads. External tables avoid loading but incur query-time GCS scan costs and have no caching. Dataflow adds transformation capability but is unnecessary overhead for a straight load of already-structured Avro files.

flashcards.front: A company stores raw event logs in a BigQuery table partitioned by `event_date`.?
flashcards.back: BigQuery row access policies (introduced as row-level security) attach filter predicates to IAM principals, transparently applying a WHERE clause to every query that principal runs. Assigning `region = 'EU'` to the EU analysts' group prevents them from ever reading US rows. Policy tags control column-level access (masking/encryption), not row filtering. Authorized views work but require maintaining a separate view per region and granting access to underlying tables. BigQuery partitioning is by date or integer range, not arbitrary column values for IAM-level row restriction.

flashcards.front: A financial company needs to train a regression model to predict loan default pr?
flashcards.back: BigQuery ML allows data analysts to create and train models using SQL inside BigQuery, with no need to export data or write Python/TensorFlow code. `CREATE MODEL ... OPTIONS(model_type='LOGISTIC_REG')` trains a logistic regression directly on BigQuery tables. Vertex AI Workbench and custom training containers require ML engineering code. Dataflow is a data processing framework, not a model training platform.

nodes.title: Dataflow: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Dataflow. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: A streaming pipeline built on Dataflow ingests IoT sensor readings from 10,000 d?
flashcards.back: Session windows group events separated by gaps smaller than a defined timeout. With a 90-second gap timeout keyed per device, each continuous burst of sensor data forms one session, and silence for 90+ seconds closes the window. Fixed/tumbling windows split bursts artificially at clock boundaries. Sliding windows create overlapping aggregates. Global windows with periodic triggers do not adapt to per-device activity patterns.

flashcards.front: An e-commerce company's Dataflow streaming pipeline processes order events from ?
flashcards.back: Dataflow supports horizontal autoscaling by adding workers up to maxNumWorkers. Raising this ceiling allows the pipeline to scale out during flash-sale spikes and handle 20x volume without manual changes. Switching to batch loses real-time processing. Dead-letter topics handle undeliverable messages, not throughput lag. Message ordering keys serialize delivery per key, which would worsen throughput under spike conditions.

flashcards.front: A startup ingests clickstream events into Pub/Sub and processes them with a Data?
flashcards.back: Apache Beam / Dataflow supports allowed lateness on event-time windows. Setting allowed lateness to 2 hours means the window will continue to accept late elements arriving up to 2 hours after the watermark passes the window end. Combined with an accumulating (or accumulating+retracting) trigger, the pipeline emits updated aggregates as late data arrives. Processing-time windows lose event-time accuracy. Re-reading a Pub/Sub topic after window close is not a reliable pattern. BigQuery UPDATE-based correction is complex and expensive.

flashcards.front: A telecom company needs to detect anomalous call patterns in real time. Their Da?
flashcards.back: Allowed lateness in Apache Beam permits elements whose event timestamp falls in an already-closed window to be assigned to that window and update the result. For a call that started in window W but whose end event arrives after the watermark passes the end of W, allowed lateness (e.g., 10 minutes) ensures it updates window W rather than being discarded. Global windows with count triggers ignore event-time semantics entirely. Sliding windows create overlapping aggregates, double-counting calls. Side inputs provide lookup enrichment, not late-data handling.

nodes.title: Vertex Ai: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Vertex Ai. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: A machine learning team needs to share engineered features — such as user purcha?
flashcards.back: Vertex AI Feature Store is designed to solve the training-serving skew problem by providing a single source of truth for features used in both model training and online serving. It stores feature values, provides low-latency online serving via the Feature Store API, and supports batch serving for training data consistency. BigQuery queries during inference add latency unsuitable for online predictions. Cloud Storage Parquet files are batch-oriented and cannot serve point lookups with millisecond latency. Pub/Sub is a messaging system, not a feature store. and serve features online via the Feature Store API

flashcards.front: A fraud detection model deployed on Vertex AI Prediction needs to be retrained w?
flashcards.back: Vertex AI Pipelines (built on KFP) is the recommended MLOps orchestration service on GCP. Each step (data validation, feature engineering, training, evaluation, deployment) is a pipeline component, and conditional logic controls deployment based on evaluation metrics. The pipeline is registered in Vertex AI and can be triggered on a schedule via Cloud Scheduler. Cloud Functions chained by Cloud Scheduler lack conditional branching and pipeline artifact tracking. Cloud Composer is a general workflow orchestrator — valid but less integrated with Vertex AI than Vertex AI Pipelines. BigQuery scheduled queries are for SQL transformations, not ML pipeline orchestration.

flashcards.front: A data science team trains a TensorFlow model on Vertex AI custom training. Afte?
flashcards.back: Vertex AI Experiments records metrics, parameters, and artifacts for each training run, enabling side-by-side comparison. Vertex AI Model Registry stores model versions with lineage, evaluation metadata, and deployment history. Together they provide a complete MLOps versioning and promotion workflow. Cloud Storage object versioning stores files but provides no metrics comparison or deployment integration. Artifact Registry Docker tags track container versions, not ML model evaluation metrics. A BigQuery metrics table is a custom solution that does not integrate with Vertex AI's deployment pipeline.

flashcards.front: A retail company wants to predict customer churn using 20 features from BigQuery?
flashcards.back: Vertex AI AutoML Tabular accepts a BigQuery table as input and automatically handles feature preprocessing, algorithm selection (neural architecture search, gradient boosted trees, etc.), and hyperparameter tuning to find the best model. Results include feature importance and evaluation metrics. BigQuery ML AUTOML_CLASSIFIER is a valid option that also runs AutoML from SQL, but Vertex AI AutoML provides more advanced tuning and a richer evaluation UI. Vertex AI Workbench with TPOT requires writing Python code. A hyperparameter tuning job requires a custom training script.

nodes.title: Mixed Topics: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Mixed Topics. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: A media company stores user engagement events in Bigtable with row keys formatte?
flashcards.back: Bigtable stores rows in sorted order; sequential or repeated-prefix keys concentrate writes on the same tablet (hot spot). Prepending a hash-derived salt (e.g., 2-byte prefix derived from hashing user_id) distributes the key space evenly across tablets, eliminating the hot spot. Auto-increment integers create a new sequential hot spot at the current highest value. Appending a region field does not change the leading prefix distribution. Reordering to event_type first moves the hot spot to the most popular event type.

flashcards.front: A data platform team has a Bigtable cluster serving read-heavy workloads for a g?
flashcards.back: Bigtable supports multi-cluster replication within an instance. By adding a second cluster in the EU region and configuring the Bigtable client with a multi-cluster routing profile (route to any cluster), reads automatically fail over to the available cluster if one cluster is in maintenance. Backups require manual restore and have high RTO. Cloud Spanner is not a drop-in for Bigtable and is designed for relational workloads. Dual independent instances require application-layer writes to both, which is complex and error-prone. and configure client routing to use the closest available cluster

flashcards.front: A gaming company stores player leaderboard data in Bigtable. A single global lea?
flashcards.back: Bigtable hot spots on a single row key cannot be resolved by adding nodes because all writes to a single key are routed to one tablet. The standard pattern is to shard the row into multiple keys using a prefix (shard_00 to shard_99), distributing writes across 100 tablets. At read time, all shards are fetched and merged. Cloud Spanner does not eliminate single-key hot spots either — it also routes all mutations to a single split leader for a given key range. Adding Bigtable nodes increases throughput per tablet but does not help a single-row hot spot. Redis Sorted Sets are a valid alternative for leaderboards but constitute a service migration, not a Bigtable row key fix. for example, `shard_00#global_leaderboard` through `shard_99#global_leaderboard` — and merge shards at read time

flashcards.front: A machine learning team stores 1,000 feature vectors per user in Bigtable for re?
flashcards.back: Bigtable read latency during peak traffic typically indicates CPU or I/O saturation on the existing nodes. Adding cluster nodes distributes tablet serving across more nodes, reducing CPU load and I/O per node, directly improving read latency. Gzip compression adds decompression CPU overhead that can worsen latency for sub-5ms requirements. Adding a second cluster adds capacity but is a larger change — horizontal scaling within one cluster is simpler and immediate. Firestore is not optimized for high-dimensional vector lookups and has different latency characteristics.
